tagline: World's second largest steel producer with inconsistent decarbonization strategy and shareholder prioritization
hero_kpi_rationale: The Capex KPI reflects the company's real commitment to decarbonization, a central issue for the steel sector. Actual decarbonization investments (USD 500M over 2021-2023) remain significantly lower than dividends paid (USD 11B), revealing a priority given to shareholders rather than climate transformation. This contrast highlights the gap between leadership promises and concrete actions.

kpis.name: Decarbonization investments
kpis.explanation: Annual actual spending dedicated to decarbonization projects and technological transformation.
kpis.description: Between 2021 and 2023, ArcelorMittal invested only USD 500 million in decarbonization, representing one-third of its initial plans, while USD 11 billion was distributed to shareholders.
kpis.signal: Decarbonization investments 22x lower than dividends paid (2021-2023)

kpis.name: Consolidated carbon footprint
kpis.explanation: Annual carbon footprint in CO2 equivalent of all group operations.
kpis.description: The 2023 carbon burden of 114.3 MtCO2e represents approximately 7% of annual global greenhouse gas emissions, before even accounting for emissions related to metallurgical coal mining extraction.
kpis.signal: Carbon footprint comparable to a country like Belgium, representing 7% of annual global emissions

kpis.name: Carbon intensity
kpis.explanation: Tonnes of CO2 equivalent emitted per tonne of crude steel produced.
kpis.description: ArcelorMittal committed to reducing its carbon intensity by 25% by 2030 versus a 2018 baseline, but this target is not aligned with a 1.5C climate scenario and lacks scientific validation according to the Science-Based Targets initiative.
kpis.signal: 25% reduction target by 2030 insufficient for a 1.5C scenario

kpis.name: Total workforce
kpis.description: ArcelorMittal employs approximately 126,756 people as of December 31, 2023, distributed across 19 countries and facing significant energy transition risks.
kpis.signal: Large workforce base requiring just transition for decarbonization

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.description: ArcelorMittal generated USD 68.3 billion in revenue in 2023, providing an adequate financial base for energy transition investments, although distributions to shareholders significantly exceed decarbonization investments.
kpis.signal: Sufficient financial resources to accelerate decarbonization but priority given to shareholders

kpis.name: Steel production
kpis.explanation: Annual crude steel production volume of the group.
kpis.description: ArcelorMittal produced approximately 58 million tonnes of steel in 2023, confirming its position as the world's second largest producer. This production relies heavily on coal-based processes that require urgent transformation.
kpis.signal: Massive production requiring accelerated technological transformation and end of coal reliance

kpis.name: Shareholder distributions
kpis.explanation: Total amount paid to shareholders through share buybacks and dividends.
kpis.description: Between 2021 and 2023, ArcelorMittal distributed USD 11 billion to shareholders, compared to only USD 500 million invested in decarbonization. This 22:1 ratio reveals strategic priorities clearly misaligned with declared climate challenges.

kpis.name: Total assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of EUR 97.7B in the last year

kpis.name: Decarbonization investments
kpis.explanation: Actual investments dedicated to decarbonization projects and innovative technologies.
kpis.description: Between 2021 and 2023, ArcelorMittal invested only USD 500 million in decarbonization, representing one-third of its initial plans. This figure contrasts sharply with the USD 11 billion distributed to shareholders, demonstrating a priority given to financial returns rather than climate transition.

ai_positioning.summary: ArcelorMittal does not mention any strategy or initiatives related to artificial intelligence in the climate assessment provided. The company does not position AI as a technological lever for its transformation or competitiveness.
evidence: No mention of AI or machine learning in the document
No reference to AI tools for process optimization or decarbonization
Complete absence of use cases or AI partnerships
